+# Karttunen's divisor numerator parity identity
+
+## Abstract
+
+Karttunen's A378444 divisor count equals the ceiling of half A174273.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The rational prime-exponent sum).**
+
+$$\forall n \in Nat,\; \operatorname{r}\left(n\right) = \operatorname{Finsupp}.\operatorname{sum}\left(\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{factorization}\left(n\right), (fun (p:Nat) \mapsto (fun (e:Nat) \mapsto \frac{(e:Rat)}{(p:Rat)}))\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/Divisors/OeisA378444DivisorNumeratorParity.r` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Antti Karttunen (2025). *OEIS A378444: divisors with even reduced prime-exponent-sum numerator*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A378444>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+OEIS A083345, NAME, revision 68 (unpaginated): “Numerator of r(n) = Sum(e/p: n=Product(p^e)); a(n) = n' / gcd(n,n'), where n' is the arithmetic derivative of n.” The function r is the displayed rational sum. Finsupp.sum ranges over the support of Nat.factorization; both casts in each quotient are to Rat. The empty sum gives r(1) = 0.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The reduced numerator).**
+
+$$\forall n \in Nat,\; \operatorname{A083345}\left(n\right) = \operatorname{Rat}.\operatorname{num}\left(\operatorname{r}\left(n\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/Divisors/OeisA378444DivisorNumeratorParity.A083345` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Antti Karttunen (2025). *OEIS A378444: divisors with even reduced prime-exponent-sum numerator*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A378444>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+OEIS A378444, NAME, revision 14 (unpaginated): “a(n) is the number of divisors d of n such that A083345(d) is even, where A083345(n) is the numerator of Sum(e/p: n=Product(p^e)).” Rat.num is the reduced numerator with positive denominator, including Rat.num 0 = 0.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (Divisors with even numerator).**
+
+$$\forall n \in Nat,\; \operatorname{A378444}\left(n\right) = \operatorname{Finset}.\operatorname{card}\left(\operatorname{Finset}.\operatorname{filter}\left((fun (d:Nat) \mapsto \operatorname{A083345}\left(d\right) \bmod 2 = 0), \operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{divisors}\left(n\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/Divisors/OeisA378444DivisorNumeratorParity.A378444` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Antti Karttunen (2025). *OEIS A378444: divisors with even reduced prime-exponent-sum numerator*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A378444>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+OEIS A378444, NAME, revision 14 (unpaginated): “a(n) is the number of divisors d of n such that A083345(d) is even, where A083345(n) is the numerator of Sum(e/p: n=Product(p^e)).” For n ≥ 1, Nat.divisors contains exactly the positive divisors. In particular d = 1 is counted because its numerator is zero. The residue here is an integer residue modulo 2.
+
+**Definition 1.4 (Parity of the exponent at two).**
+
+$$\forall n \in Nat,\; \operatorname{A035263}\left(n\right) = if (\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{factorization}\left(n, 2\right) \bmod 2 = 0) then 1 else 0$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/Divisors/OeisA378444DivisorNumeratorParity.A035263` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Antti Karttunen (2025). *OEIS A378444: divisors with even reduced prime-exponent-sum numerator*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A378444>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+OEIS A035263, COMMENT, revision 266 (unpaginated): “a(n) is 1 if the number of trailing zeros in the binary representation of n is even.” For positive n this is the parity of Nat.factorization n 2. The residue here is a natural residue modulo 2.
+
+**Definition 1.5 (The divisor transform).**
+
+$$\forall n \in Nat,\; \operatorname{A174273}\left(n\right) = \operatorname{Finset}.\operatorname{sum}\left(\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{divisors}\left(n\right), (fun (d:Nat) \mapsto \operatorname{A035263}\left(d\right))\right)$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/Divisors/OeisA378444DivisorNumeratorParity.A174273` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Antti Karttunen (2025). *OEIS A378444: divisors with even reduced prime-exponent-sum numerator*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A378444>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+OEIS A174273, NAME, revision 17 (unpaginated): “Inverse Moebius transform of A035263.” This is the sum of A035263 over the positive divisors for n ≥ 1.
+
+**Definition 1.6 (Karttunen's ceiling conjecture).**
+
+$$claim = (\forall n \in Nat,\; (1 \le n) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{A378444}\left(n\right) = \operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{ceil}\left(\frac{(\operatorname{A174273}\left(n\right):Rat)}{2}\right)))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/Divisors/OeisA378444DivisorNumeratorParity.claim` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Antti Karttunen (2025). *OEIS A378444: divisors with even reduced prime-exponent-sum numerator*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A378444>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+OEIS A378444, FORMULA, revision 14 (unpaginated): “a(n) = ceiling(A174273(n)/2). [Conjectured] - _Antti Karttunen_, May 14 2025”. Its offset is 1. The variable n ranges over Nat with 1 ≤ n. The cast to Rat precedes division by 2; Nat.ceil equals the ordinary ceiling of this nonnegative rational.
+
+**Theorem 1.7 (The ceiling identity holds for every positive integer).**
+
+$$\forall n \in Nat,\; (1 \le n) \Rightarrow (\operatorname{A378444}\left(n\right) = \operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{ceil}\left(\frac{(\operatorname{A174273}\left(n\right):Rat)}{2}\right))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Divisors/OeisA378444DivisorNumeratorParity.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Resolves.* `Problems/karttunen-a378444` (proved) by `D5/S3/Arith/Divisors/OeisA378444DivisorNumeratorParity.result`.
+
+<!-- scribe-open-problem-resolution-v1 {"problem_slug":"karttunen-a378444","declaration_gid":"D5/S3/Arith/Divisors/OeisA378444DivisorNumeratorParity.result","resolution_kind":"proved"} -->
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Antti Karttunen (2025). *OEIS A378444: divisors with even reduced prime-exponent-sum numerator*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A378444>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Write a divisor as 2^a times a product of odd prime powers. An odd common denominator shows that its reduced numerator is even exactly when a is even and a/2 plus the sum of the odd-prime exponents is even. Halving the even exponent at 2 identifies these divisors with exponent vectors in a finite rectangular box. The alternating sign sum of that box is a product of zeros and ones, so the number of even exponent sums is the ceiling of half its size. This includes 1, odd integers, powers of two and arbitrary mixed prime powers. The proof uses the inverse Moebius transform definition of A174273.
+
+## References
+

+import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Factorization.Defs
+import Mathlib.NumberTheory.Divisors
+import Mathlib.Data.Rat.Floor
+
+import Mathlib.Data.Finsupp.Interval
+import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.BigOperators.Ring.Finset
+import Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.GeomSum
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
+
+namespace D5.S3.Arith.Divisors.OeisA378444DivisorNumeratorParity
+
+/-- A083345: r(n) = Sum(e/p: n=Product(p^e)), for positive n. -/
+def r (n : ℕ) : ℚ :=
+  n.factorization.sum (fun p e => (e : ℚ) / (p : ℚ))
+
+/-- The numerator in the reduced rational representation, including num(0)=0. -/
+def A083345 (n : ℕ) : ℤ := (r n).num
+
+/-- A378444: number of positive divisors with even A083345 value. -/
+def A378444 (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
+  (n.divisors.filter (fun d => A083345 d % 2 = 0)).card
+
+/-- A035263: 1 for an even number of binary trailing zeros, and 0 otherwise. -/
+def A035263 (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
+  if n.factorization 2 % 2 = 0 then 1 else 0
+
+/-- A174273: the inverse Moebius transform of A035263. -/
+def A174273 (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
+  ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, A035263 d
+
+/-- A378444 FORMULA, Karttunen's unnumbered ceiling conjecture. -/
+def claim : Prop :=
+  ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → A378444 n = ⌈(A174273 n : ℚ) / 2⌉₊
+
+open Finset
+set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000
+
+private theorem odd_den_num_parity (q : ℚ) (N D : ℤ) (hD : Odd D)
+    (hq : q = (N : ℚ) / D) : q.num % 2 = N % 2 := by
+  have hd : D ≠ 0 := by
+    have := Int.odd_iff.mp hD
+    omega
+  have hdiv : q = Rat.divInt N D := by simpa only [Rat.divInt_eq_div] using hq
+  obtain ⟨c, hN, hc⟩ := Rat.num_den_mk hd hdiv
+  have hcodd : c % 2 = 1 := by
+    have hmod := congrArg (fun x : ℤ => x % 2) hc
+    have hDmod : D % 2 = 1 := Int.odd_iff.mp hD
+    by_contra hh
+    have hc0 : c % 2 = 0 := by exact Int.emod_two_ne_one.mp hh
+    simp only [Int.mul_emod, hc0, zero_mul, Int.zero_emod] at hmod
+    omega
+  rw [hN, Int.mul_emod, hcodd]
+  omega
+
+private theorem numerator_parity (a N D : ℕ) (hD : Odd D) :
+    (((a : ℚ) / 2 + (N : ℚ) / D).num % 2 = 0) ↔
+      a % 2 = 0 ∧ (a / 2 + N) % 2 = 0 := by
+  have hD0 : (D : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (show D ≠ 0 from by have := Nat.odd_iff.mp hD; omega)
+  by_cases ha : a % 2 = 0
+  · have hsplit : (a : ℚ) / 2 + (N : ℚ) / D =
+        ((a / 2 * D + N : ℕ) : ℚ) / D := by
+      have ha' : a = a / 2 * 2 := by omega
+      conv_lhs => lhs; rw [ha']
+      push_cast
+      field_simp
+
+    rw [odd_den_num_parity _ ((a / 2 * D + N : ℕ) : ℤ) (D : ℤ) (by exact_mod_cast hD) (by exact_mod_cast hsplit)]
+    have hDm : D % 2 = 1 := Nat.odd_iff.mp hD
+    norm_cast
+    simp [ha, Nat.add_mod, Nat.mul_mod, hDm]
+  · have hm : (a * D + 2 * N) % 2 = 1 := by
+      have hDm : D % 2 = 1 := Nat.odd_iff.mp hD
+      simp [Nat.add_mod, Nat.mul_mod, hDm]
+      omega
+    have hsplit : (a : ℚ) / 2 + (N : ℚ) / D =
+        ((a * D + 2 * N : ℕ) : ℚ) / (2 * D) := by
+      push_cast
+      field_simp
+
+    have hdiv : (a : ℚ) / 2 + (N : ℚ) / D =
+        Rat.divInt (a * D + 2 * N : ℤ) (2 * D) := by
+      simpa only [Rat.divInt_eq_div, Int.cast_add, Int.cast_mul, Int.cast_ofNat,
+        Int.cast_natCast, Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_mul, Nat.cast_ofNat] using hsplit
+    have hdvd := Rat.num_dvd (a * D + 2 * N : ℤ) (show (2 * D : ℤ) ≠ 0 by
+      exact mul_ne_zero (by norm_num) (by exact_mod_cast (show D ≠ 0 from by have := Nat.odd_iff.mp hD; omega)))
+    rw [← hdiv] at hdvd
+    constructor
+    · intro h
+      obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hdvd
+      have he := congrArg (fun z : ℤ => z % 2) hk
+      rw [Int.mul_emod, h] at he
+      norm_cast at he
+      omega
+    · simp [ha]
+
+private theorem odd_sum_rep (s : Finset ℕ) (f : ℕ → ℕ)
+    (hs : ∀ p ∈ s, Odd p) :
+    ∃ N D : ℕ, Odd D ∧ (∑ p ∈ s, (f p : ℚ) / p) = (N : ℚ) / D ∧
+      N % 2 = (∑ p ∈ s, f p) % 2 := by
+  classical
+  induction s using Finset.induction with
+  | empty => exact ⟨0, 1, by simp, by simp, by simp⟩
+  | insert p s hp ih =>
+    obtain ⟨N, D, hD, hq, hN⟩ := ih (fun q hq => hs q (by simp [hq]))
+    have hop := hs p (mem_insert_self _ _)
+    have hp0 : (p : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by
+      have hm := Nat.odd_iff.mp hop
+      exact_mod_cast (show p ≠ 0 from by omega)
+    have hD0 : (D : ℚ) ≠ 0 := by
+      have hm := Nat.odd_iff.mp hD
+      exact_mod_cast (show D ≠ 0 from by omega)
+    refine ⟨f p * D + N * p, p * D, hop.mul hD, ?_, ?_⟩
+    · rw [sum_insert hp, hq]
+      push_cast
+      field_simp
+    · rw [sum_insert hp]
+      simp only [Nat.add_mod, Nat.mul_mod, Nat.odd_iff.mp hop, Nat.odd_iff.mp hD,
+        mul_one, hN, Nat.mod_mod]
+
+private theorem r_parity (n : ℕ) : A083345 n % 2 = 0 ↔
+    n.factorization 2 % 2 = 0 ∧
+      (n.factorization 2 / 2 + (n.factorization.erase 2).sum (fun _ e => e)) % 2 = 0 := by
+  classical
+  obtain ⟨N, D, hD, hq, hN⟩ := odd_sum_rep (n.factorization.erase 2).support
+    (n.factorization.erase 2) (by
+      intro p hp
+      have hp' : p ∈ n.primeFactors := by
+        have := (Finset.mem_erase.mp (by simpa only [Finsupp.support_erase] using hp)).2
+        exact this
+      exact (Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors hp').odd_of_ne_two
+        (by
+          exact (Finset.mem_erase.mp (by simpa only [Finsupp.support_erase] using hp)).1))
+  have hr : r n = (n.factorization 2 : ℚ) / 2 + (N : ℚ) / D := by
+    rw [r, ← hq]
+    exact (Finsupp.add_sum_erase' n.factorization 2 (fun p e => (e : ℚ) / p)
+      (by simp)).symm
+  rw [A083345, hr, numerator_parity _ _ _ hD]
+  change _ ↔ _ ∧ (_ + ∑ p ∈ (n.factorization.erase 2).support, _) % 2 = 0
+  simp only [Nat.add_mod, hN, Nat.mod_mod]
+
+private noncomputable def halfExp (f : ℕ →₀ ℕ) : ℕ →₀ ℕ := f.update 2 (f 2 / 2)
+private noncomputable def doubleExp (f : ℕ →₀ ℕ) : ℕ →₀ ℕ := f.update 2 (2 * f 2)
+
+private theorem halfExp_sum (f : ℕ →₀ ℕ) :
+    (halfExp f).sum (fun _ e => e) = f 2 / 2 + (f.erase 2).sum (fun _ e => e) := by
+  simpa [halfExp, Finsupp.update_apply] using
+    (Finsupp.add_sum_erase' (halfExp f) 2 (fun _ e => e) (by simp)).symm
+
+private theorem compressed_card (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0) (P : (ℕ →₀ ℕ) → Prop)
+    [DecidablePred P] :
+    (n.divisors.filter (fun d => d.factorization 2 % 2 = 0 ∧ P (halfExp d.factorization))).card =
+    ((Finset.Iic (halfExp n.factorization)).filter P).card := by
+  classical
+  apply Finset.card_bij (fun d hd => halfExp d.factorization)
+  · intro d hd
+    obtain ⟨hdmem, he, hP⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hd
+    apply Finset.mem_filter.mpr
+    refine ⟨Finset.mem_Iic.mpr ?_, hP⟩
+    have hd0 := ne_zero_of_dvd_ne_zero hn (Nat.dvd_of_mem_divisors hdmem)
+    have hle := (Nat.factorization_le_iff_dvd hd0 hn).mpr (Nat.dvd_of_mem_divisors hdmem)
+    intro p
+    by_cases hp : p = 2
+    · subst p
+      simpa [halfExp, Finsupp.update_apply] using Nat.div_le_div_right (hle 2)
+    · simpa [halfExp, Finsupp.update_apply, hp] using hle p
+  · intro d hd e he hde
+    obtain ⟨hdmem, hd2, hdP⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hd
+    obtain ⟨hemem, he2, heP⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp he
+    apply Nat.eq_of_factorization_eq' (ne_zero_of_dvd_ne_zero hn (Nat.dvd_of_mem_divisors hdmem))
+      (ne_zero_of_dvd_ne_zero hn (Nat.dvd_of_mem_divisors hemem))
+    ext p
+    have h := congrArg (fun f : ℕ →₀ ℕ => f p) hde
+    by_cases hp : p = 2
+    · subst p
+      simp [halfExp, Finsupp.update_apply] at h
+      omega
+    · simpa [halfExp, Finsupp.update_apply, hp] using h
+  · intro f hf
+    obtain ⟨hfmem, hP⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hf
+    have hle : doubleExp f ≤ n.factorization := by
+      intro p
+      have h := (Finset.mem_Iic.mp hfmem) p
+      by_cases hp : p = 2
+      · subst p
+        simp [doubleExp, halfExp, Finsupp.update_apply] at h ⊢
+        omega
+      · simpa [doubleExp, halfExp, Finsupp.update_apply, hp] using h
+    let d := (doubleExp f).prod (fun p e => p ^ e)
+    have hdvd : d ∣ n := Nat.prod_pow_dvd_of_le_factorization hle
+    have hfact : d.factorization = doubleExp f := Nat.factorization_prod_pow_eq_self_of_le_factorization hle
+    have hhalf : halfExp d.factorization = f := by
+      rw [hfact]
+      simp [halfExp, doubleExp, Finsupp.update_apply]
+    refine ⟨d, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Nat.mem_divisors.mpr ⟨hdvd, hn⟩, ?_, ?_⟩, hhalf⟩
+    · rw [hfact]
+      simp [doubleExp, Finsupp.update_apply]
+    · rwa [hhalf]
+
+private theorem box_eq (f : ℕ →₀ ℕ) :
+    Finset.Iic f = f.support.finsupp (fun p => Finset.range (f p + 1)) := by
+  classical
+  rw [Finset.Iic_eq_Icc, show (⊥ : ℕ →₀ ℕ) = 0 from rfl, Finsupp.Icc_eq]
+  simp only [Finsupp.support_zero, Finset.empty_union]
+  congr 1
+  funext p
+  simp [Nat.range_succ_eq_Icc_zero]
+
+private theorem box_sign_sum (f : ℕ →₀ ℕ) :
+    (∑ g ∈ Finset.Iic f, (-1 : ℤ) ^ (g.sum (fun _ e => e))) =
+      ∏ p ∈ f.support, (if Even (f p + 1) then (0 : ℤ) else 1) := by
+  classical
+  let : DecidableEq ℕ := Classical.decEq ℕ
+  rw [box_eq, Finset.finsupp, Finset.sum_map]
+  simp only [Function.Embedding.coeFn_mk]
+  simp_rw [Finsupp.sum_indicator_index_eq_sum_attach (h := fun (_ : ℕ) (e : ℕ) => e) _ (fun _ _ => rfl),
+    ← Finset.prod_pow_eq_pow_sum]
+  have h := Finset.prod_sum f.support (fun p => range (f p + 1))
+    (fun (_ : ℕ) (b : ℕ) => (-1 : ℤ) ^ b)
+  simp only [neg_one_geom_sum] at h
+  exact h.symm
+
+private theorem box_balance (f : ℕ →₀ ℕ) :
+    0 ≤ (∑ g ∈ Finset.Iic f, (-1 : ℤ) ^ (g.sum (fun _ e => e))) ∧
+    (∑ g ∈ Finset.Iic f, (-1 : ℤ) ^ (g.sum (fun _ e => e))) ≤ 1 := by
+  rw [box_sign_sum]
+  constructor
+  · exact Finset.prod_nonneg (fun p hp => by split_ifs <;> norm_num)
+  · exact Finset.prod_le_one₀ (fun p hp => by split_ifs <;> norm_num)

+# Karttunen's A378444 divisor-numerator parity formula
+
+## Problem
+
+OEIS A378444 states the unnumbered FORMULA conjecture
+
+$$
+\forall n\in\mathbb{N},\quad 1\le n\Rightarrow
+\operatorname{A378444}(n)=\left\lceil\frac{\operatorname{A174273}(n)}{2}\right\rceil.
+$$
+
+Here $\operatorname{A378444}(n)$ counts positive divisors whose reduced
+numerator $\operatorname{A083345}(d)$ is even, and $\operatorname{A174273}$ is
+the divisor sum of the indicator that the exponent of 2 in the factorization
+is even. The exact Lean proposition is `claim` in the settling module.
+
+### Statement echo
+
+The source's divisor condition is mirrored by `A378444`; the reduced numerator
+is `A083345`; the parity indicator is `A035263`; and the divisor transform is
+`A174273`. The positivity restriction is the hypothesis `1 ≤ n`. The ceiling
+is taken after casting `A174273 n` to rationals and dividing by two.
+
+## Motivation
+
+The formula asserts an exact identity for every positive integer, including
+the boundary value $1$, odd integers, powers of two, and mixed prime powers.
+The source and preregistration are issue [#23534](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/23534).
+
+## Gap
+
+The source records the identity as conjectured. The bounded literature screen
+associated with #23534 found no complete prior proof in its searched scope.
+Completeness of that screen and originality beyond the retained source are
+`ASSUMED-UNVERIFIED`.
+
+## Route
+
+For a divisor, write the exponent at two as $a$ and the remaining prime
+exponents as a finitely supported function. An odd common denominator gives
+the reduced-numerator parity criterion
+
+$$
+\operatorname{A083345}(d)\equiv 0\pmod 2
+\Longleftrightarrow
+a\equiv 0\pmod 2\ \wedge\ (a/2+\sum_{p\ne2}e_p)\equiv0\pmod2.
+$$
+
+Halving the even exponent at two bijects the selected divisors with the even
+parity part of a finite exponent box. The alternating sum over that box
+factors into one-dimensional geometric sums, so its value lies between zero
+and one. This forces the even-parity count to be the ceiling of half the box
+size. The inverse divisor transform identifies that box size with
+$\operatorname{A174273}(n)$.
+
+## Falsifier
+
+A positive integer $n$ for which the divisor count and the stated ceiling
+differ would refute `claim`. A failure of the reduced-numerator parity
+criterion, the divisor-box bijection, or the alternating-sum bound would
+invalidate the proof route.
